references.text: Deborah called Barak, son of Abinoam, to lead Israel's army against Sisera, which is the background for the song of victory in chapter 5.
Deborah said to Barak: 'Arise!' - the same call as in the song where she urges Barak to rise and take captives.
The cry 'Wake up!' is also used in the Psalms as a plea to God to intervene and act for His people.
David uses similar language when he urges his soul to wake up to praise the Lord.
Isaiah uses the same expression 'Awake, awake' as a call for the arm of the Lord to act with power.
Isaiah uses a double 'awake' addressed to Zion, echoing Deborah's call to awaken in the song.
Paul quotes a similar call to awaken: 'Wake up, you who sleep, arise from the dead' - the same pattern of repeated calls to wake and rise.
